name: Eleventh Dream Day
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: A Louisville punk house, a husband-and-wife core, a seven-record Atlantic contract that stopped at three albums, and forty years of guitars turned up well past polite.

eras.title: Out of 1069 Bardstown Road
eras.text: Eleventh Dream Day came out of a Louisville punk house at 1069 Bardstown Road and landed in Chicago. Rick Rizzo's guitar leaned on Neil Young, Janet Beveridge Bean moved behind the drums, and a one-night session in a Louisville studio got them noticed by the majors.

years.h: Rick Rizzo and Janet Bean start Eleventh Dream Day in Chicago
years.p: Rick Rizzo and Janet Beveridge Bean met at 1069 Bardstown Road, a Louisville punk house where Bean played in the Zoo Directors with [[Tara Key|c75b1d24-3127-4dba-88d2-40a263995b1d]]. Rizzo talked Bean into moving to Chicago; Shu Shubat played bass.
years.xp: Comedy Minus One, the band's later label, calls 1069 Bardstown Road a punk rock think tank. Rizzo and Bean started the band in Chicago and eventually married. Bean first played guitar, then moved to drums, where she stayed, singing from behind the kit.

years.h: Doug McCombs and Baird Figi lock in the classic line-up
years.p: Bassist [[Doug McCombs|2bf77a32-29bb-432f-afe1-bde92b431c23]] replaces Shu Shubat and guitarist [[Baird Figi|f294e1ac-58bf-4355-925a-8c9875c155f4]] joins Rick Rizzo and Janet Bean. Comedy Minus One's bio sums them up as a fly fisherman and a body-builder.

years.h: Eleventh Dream Day EP · Amoeba Records
years.p: Eleventh Dream Day's first record, a self-titled EP on Amoeba Records, sets the template: Neil Young-style guitar workouts played with punk speed.

years.h: 15 songs, one night, one buzzing amp: Prairie School Freakout
years.p: Eleventh Dream Day record Prairie School Freakout at Artist Recording Service in Louisville between 11 pm and 5 am. Half the night went to fighting a buzz in Rick Rizzo's amp.
years.xp: The liner notes tell it: fifteen songs in six hours, half of that spent trying to kill the hum coming out of Rizzo's amplifier. They gave up and made amp buzz the theme of the record. The band co-produced with Louisville guitarist [[Wink O'Bannon|c8e17b50-f4f9-4151-9946-5fad012dce04]], who would join Eleventh Dream Day five years later.

years.h: Prairie School Freakout · Amoeba Records
years.p: Eleventh Dream Day's first album comes out on Amoeba, and the majors start calling. Spin later put it on its list of 80 excellent records of the 1980s.
years.xp: Critics lined up behind Prairie School Freakout. Greg Kot called it both steeped in tradition and ahead of its time. Jim DeRogatis called it the band's masterpiece, and AllMusic said Eleventh Dream Day never rocked harder. Thrill Jockey reissued it in 2003 with the Wayne EP and the band's music videos.

eras.title: Seven records promised
eras.text: Atlantic Records signed Eleventh Dream Day to a seven-record contract. They got three albums out of it, two modern rock chart singles, and a line-up change, then Atlantic let them go and the band made its favorite record on an indie.

years.h: Atlantic signs Eleventh Dream Day for seven records
years.p: On the strength of the debut EP and Prairie School Freakout, Atlantic Records chases Eleventh Dream Day and offers a seven-record contract, according to Comedy Minus One's band bio.

years.h: Beet · Atlantic, cut in four days
years.p: Eleventh Dream Day's major-label debut is recorded in four days in June 1989 with producer Gary Waleik. The Chicago Reader called it a hoot; Robert Christgau gave it a C+.

years.h: Testify reaches No. 26 on the modern rock chart
years.p: Testify, from Eleventh Dream Day's Beet, climbs to No. 26 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart. Atlantic also presses Borscht, a promo-only release.

years.h: Lived to Tell · Atlantic
years.p: Eleventh Dream Day's second Atlantic album. Its single Rose of Jericho reaches No. 27 on the Modern Rock chart.

years.h: Baird Figi quits; Wink O'Bannon joins on guitar
years.p: Guitarist Baird Figi leaves Eleventh Dream Day. Matthew "Wink" O'Bannon, who co-produced Prairie School Freakout back in Louisville, becomes the second guitarist.

years.h: El Moodio · made twice, in Chicago and New York
years.p: Eleventh Dream Day start El Moodio in Chicago with [[Brad Wood|58c8c056-4f9a-4a3b-8dd9-69b06bb23c28]], then remake it at Sorcerer Sound in New York with producer Jim Rondinelli for Atlantic.
years.xp: Rick Rizzo and Janet Bean wrote nine of the ten songs; Wink O'Bannon brought Murder. [[Velvet Crush|dadd10f1-9db4-4a35-b939-9469029deab5]]'s Ric Menck drums on That's the Point. The shelved Chicago sessions with Brad Wood at Idful finally came out in 2013 as New Moodio.

years.h: Atlantic drops Eleventh Dream Day after El Moodio
years.p: El Moodio was Eleventh Dream Day's shot at a commercial record. It didn't sell, and Atlantic dropped the band after three albums of a seven-record deal.
years.xp: Reviews split. Rolling Stone said the band had passion to burn; the Washington Post said the album never pulled together its Velvet Underground, Neil Young and Dream Syndicate influences. The band toured North America behind it anyway, then walked back into Chicago's indie world.

years.h: Ursa Major · the opener that named a band
years.p: Recorded at Idful in Chicago by [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] and mixed by Brad Wood for Atavistic. It opens with an instrumental called History of Brokeback, later the name of Doug McCombs's own band, [[Brokeback|e3fa3b7a-b883-4432-9152-ed0cf4d5c19c]].
years.xp: Planned as an EP, Ursa Major grew into an album and became what the band calls its collective favorite. [[Bundy K. Brown|940101f1-79c7-40ac-98d3-7b924b244a8e]] and McEntire, both in the orbit of [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]], added parts. The Chicago Tribune ranked it the ninth best album of 1994.

years.h: Wink O'Bannon leaves; the band stops going full time
years.p: Wink O'Bannon quits after Ursa Major. Rick Rizzo goes back to college for an education degree, Janet Bean puts her time into [[Freakwater|50e68a47-b6e4-4178-84d5-8955206a0b7f]], and Doug McCombs into [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]].

eras.title: Part-timers on Thrill Jockey
eras.text: Eleventh Dream Day never broke up, it just stopped being a job. Thrill Jockey, home to Tortoise and Freakwater, became home base, and the records came every few years, usually after the members' other bands allowed.

years.h: Eighth · first record for Thrill Jockey
years.p: Three years after Ursa Major, Eleventh Dream Day resurface on Thrill Jockey with Rick Rizzo, Janet Bean and Doug McCombs still at the core.

years.h: Stalled Parade · Mark Greenberg joins
years.p: [[Mark Greenberg|67e0ccc5-9dc9-4f23-b037-e94a53520563]] of [[The Coctails|0b94e13b-4ee7-448c-be31-5d125d8717ef]] joins Eleventh Dream Day on keyboards and more for Stalled Parade, their second Thrill Jockey album.

years.h: Thrill Jockey reissues Prairie School Freakout
years.p: Thrill Jockey reissues Eleventh Dream Day's 1988 album with the Wayne EP, bonus tracks including a cover of Neil Young's Southern Pacific, and the band's videos.

years.h: Zeroes and Ones · Thrill Jockey
years.p: Eleventh Dream Day's third Thrill Jockey album arrives six years after Stalled Parade.

eras.title: The Hideout years
eras.text: Eleventh Dream Day turned Chicago's Hideout into a workshop: a long residency where new songs got loud in front of people before they were recorded. A second guitarist came back for the first time since 1994, and the records got rawer.

years.h: Riot Now! · Thrill Jockey
years.p: Eleventh Dream Day's fourth Thrill Jockey album, released March 15, 2011.

years.h: James Elkington makes Eleventh Dream Day twin-guitar again
years.p: Guitarist [[James Elkington|0b4020a0-0126-4574-bbed-d9109ed60b8a]] of [[Brokeback|e3fa3b7a-b883-4432-9152-ed0cf4d5c19c]] joins. Thrill Jockey notes it's the band's first second guitarist since 1994.

years.h: New Moodio · the lost first El Moodio
years.p: Comedy Minus One releases the 1991 Chicago sessions Eleventh Dream Day cut with Brad Wood at Idful, the version of El Moodio Atlantic never put out.

years.h: Works for Tomorrow, built onstage at the Hideout
years.p: Eleventh Dream Day work up Works for Tomorrow in a long residency at Chicago's Hideout, then Mark Greenberg records it at the Loft, [[Wilco|9e53f84d-ef44-4c16-9677-5fd4d78cbd7d]]'s studio, and Mayfair Recordings.
years.xp: The five-piece of Rizzo, Bean, McCombs, Greenberg and Elkington made the record Thrill Jockey pitched as a band still fighting its own past. The label singled out Bean's singing, delivered with what it called an animalistic urgency. Critics liked it.

years.h: Since Grazed: a surprise double album
years.p: Eleventh Dream Day drop Since Grazed, a double LP on Comedy Minus One, with no warning on April 2, 2021. The label describes the band as semi-retired but still making records.
